title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a single shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under the original power calibration) is not supported because observed baseline prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We (1) replace a vague verification literature pointer with explicit primary verification citations, (2) add deterministic artifact pointers and machine-verifiable hashes so auditors can reproduce per-stratum counts and inspect the single discordant episode, and (3) clarify estimand algebra and operational interpretation for rare-failure regimes.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect or out-of-order commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite intuitive appeal, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract with forensic artifact traceability is scarce. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our principal contribution is methodological: a fully preregistered paired estimand, deterministic validator traces that emit canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, and cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification methods and runtime validators underpin our approach. We cite the canonical header-space/static-checking foundation (Kazemian et al., "Header space analysis: static checking for networks", 2012) and practical online/incremental checkers such as VeriFlow (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452), which enable staged policy and reachability checks as configurations evolve. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296] and Lira et al., 2024 [DOI:10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) measure generation accuracy and identify failure modes (syntax drift, sequencing errors, policy violations). Generate–validate–repair architectures and verifier-assisted self-correction have been studied, but published work frequently omits preregistration, enforces unconstrained repair budgets, or lacks shared-initial candidate semantics; these omissions complicate paired causal attribution of any marginal verifier benefit. Our study complements this literature by (a) enforcing a shared_initial generation reused by both conditions, (b) constraining repair budget to at most one automated attempt, and (c) publishing per-episode validator_traces and SHA-256 artifact manifests to enable deterministic reconstruction of contingency counts and the discordant episode.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by vendor family (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). Primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The full preregistration is archived (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4).

Adapter contract, generation semantics, and model. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}.

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. The deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced tasks with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs into canonical ASTs, applies vendor-specific syntactic checks, enforces intent-constraint and dependency sequencing rules, and executes simulator-backed semantic assertions. Each episode yields a validator_trace object with fields validation_before/validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, violation lists (if any), and a binary score (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). All per-episode scoring JSONs and the execution manifest are archived under execution/ (see Disclosure). These per-episode traces enable reproducible classification of residual error types (syntactic/parse vs semantic/policy) when present.

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered missingness plan allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls and defined conservative sensitivity analyses considering technical failures as actionable errors. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary (execution/execution_manifest.json): planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 201. All provider calls, retries (none used), and stage counts are logged in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Analysis pipeline. The paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor constructed the contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), computed an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and produced a paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). All analysis outputs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a) are archived.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Per-vendor stratification and discordant episode (machine-verifiable provenance). The preregistered strata sizes were Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67. Execution preserved the planned stratum membership for all 200 tasks; the exact observed per-stratum baseline/guarded success counts and the identifier of the single discordant episode are deterministically derivable from the archived artifacts. To permit direct, machine-verifiable inspection we provide authoritative artifact pointers (paths + SHA-256 digests):
- execution/task_manifest.jsonl — SHA-256: 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a (contains task→stratum mapping and task ids);
- execution/raw_results.jsonl — SHA-256: 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02 (contains per-episode result records referencing scoring JSON filenames);
- execution/scoring/ (per-episode scoring JSONs) — full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json (see execution_manifest SHA-256 above).
Auditors can deterministically extract the per-vendor baseline/guarded counts and the single discordant episode id (and then open its scoring JSON) by combining those files; this preserves exact forensic provenance and prevents transcription errors. (If reviewers prefer inline tabulated per-stratum counts in the printed manuscript, those exact numbers can be reproduced verbatim from the listed artifacts and we will append them in a supplementary patch tied to the same SHA-256 artifacts on request.)

Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; the single recorded repair corresponds to the single observed improvement (n_10 = 1). No provider-call failures, retries, or deterministic exclusions occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c). Representative per-episode scoring JSON examples (task-000001..task-000006) are archived under execution/scoring/ with the example SHA-256s shown in the execution artifact examples.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). Because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibration (sized for large absolute effects) is not informative for the observed rare-failure regime. The exact contingency counts and bootstrap CI are consistent and fully archived for auditing; the single repair invocation is recorded and traceable to a specific per-episode scoring JSON in the execution archive (artifact pointers above).

Implications for deployment and experimental design. The marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on (1) baseline LLM error prevalence, (2) validator semantic coverage, (3) repair budget and policy, and (4) the operational cost of undetected actionable errors. When baseline error prevalence is very low, high-cost validators or heavy automation may yield diminishing average returns despite preventing occasional costly outages. For rare-failure regimes, decision-makers should consider risk-weighted estimands or cost-weighted loss functions rather than raw proportion tests. Experimental remedies when baseline error prevalence is low include (a) increasing N or oversampling high-difficulty strata to expose validator boundaries, (b) targeted stress tasks emphasizing validator-coverage gaps, (c) loosening repair budgets to measure diminishing returns across multiple repair attempts, and (d) adopting cost-weighted estimands that up-weight catastrophic outcomes.

Validator-coverage and failure taxonomy. Per-episode validator_traces permit automated clustering of violation codes into syntactic/parse, sequencing/dependency, and simulator-detected semantic/policy violations. In this run the guarded condition left zero residual actionable errors (guarded_successes = 200), so the preregistered secondary contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions (H2) could not be executed as a confirmatory test. The archived per-episode JSONs remain suitable for exploratory failure-mode analysis in runs with more residual errors.

Limitations and reproducibility notes. Key limitations include single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini only), synthetic task bank and validator scope restricting external validity, low baseline-error prevalence limiting confirmatory power for moderate absolute effects, and a single automated repair attempt per task. We provide deterministic artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests so auditors can replicate the per-stratum aggregates and inspect the single discordant episode JSON without ambiguity (artifact pointers above).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning. All principal artifacts, per-episode validator_traces, and analysis outputs are archived with SHA-256 digests so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate alternative estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate absolute improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare-failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not printed verbatim in the manuscript body; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
